drug_class: Opioid analgesic combination (mixed opioid agonist-antagonist plus opioid blocker)
purpose: This medication is used to relieve moderate to severe pain. It combines a pain reliever (pentazocine) with a safety ingredient (naloxone) to help manage pain effectively. It is typically used when other pain medicines have not worked well enough.
how_it_works: Pentazocine works by attaching to special pain receptors in your brain and spinal cord, which reduces how much pain you feel. Naloxone is added as a safety measure — if the tablet is taken by mouth as prescribed, the naloxone has very little effect. However, if someone tries to inject the crushed tablet, the naloxone blocks the opioid effect and helps prevent misuse.
common_side_effects: You may feel dizzy, drowsy, or lightheaded. Nausea, vomiting, and constipation are also common. Some people experience headaches, sweating, or a feeling of confusion. These effects are usually manageable but let your doctor or pharmacist know if they bother you.
warnings: This medicine can be habit-forming, so take it exactly as prescribed and do not share it with anyone. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication — it can cause dangerous drowsiness or breathing problems. Tell your doctor if you have breathing problems, liver or kidney disease, or if you are pregnant. Stopping suddenly can cause withdrawal symptoms, so talk to your doctor before stopping.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one tablet (50 mg pentazocine / 0.5 mg naloxone) taken by mouth every 3 to 4 hours as needed for pain. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how well your pain is controlled. Do not take more than 12 tablets in a 24-hour period unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
